building_address_records.name: building_address_records
building_address_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS FACILITY_ID,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  -- Construct STREET_ADDRESS from fac_building_address components if original STREET_ADDRESS column not present.
  -- Per instructions, must expose fac_building_address.STREET_ADDRESS as selected source; that column does not exist,
  -- so we will join fac_building for BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS and also expose individual address components from fac_building_address
  -- but keep required output name STREET_ADDRESS coming from fac_building_address by returning CONCAT of its known parts.
  -- This is allowed only because fac_building_address does contain street components (STREET_NUMBER, PRE_DIRECTIONAL, STREET_NAME, STREET_SUFFIX, POST_DIRECTIONAL, STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX).
  -- Build the street address from those stored columns (do not substitute from other tables).
  CONCAT(
    NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX <> '' THEN CONCAT(fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NAME IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NAME <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_NAME) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_SUFFIX <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_SUFFIX) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL) ELSE '' END
  ) AS STREET_ADDRESS,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE,
  fba.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY
FROM fac_building_address fba
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
building_address_records.description: All building-address records including address fields and the address purpose flag.

building_basic.name: building_basic
building_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER        AS FACILITY_ID,
  b.BUILDING_KEY            AS ORG_ID
FROM fac_building AS fb
LEFT JOIN buildings AS b
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = fb.BUILDING_NUMBER
building_basic.description: One row per building with its canonical building key and links to organizational units (for joining to DLC if needed).

independent_activity_sections.name: independent_activity_sections
independent_activity_sections.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE               AS subject_title,
  so.MEET_PLACE                  AS meet_place,
  NULL                           AS term_start_date,
  CONCAT(so.SUBJECT_ID, ' ', so.COURSE_NUMBER) AS subject_label,
  so.SECTION_ID                  AS subject_offering_id,
  (CASE WHEN so.CLUSTER_TYPE = 'Independent Activity' OR so.FORM_TYPE = 'Independent Activity' OR so.IS_MASTER_SECTION = 'Y' AND so.IS_LECTURE_SECTION = 'N' AND so.IS_LAB_SECTION = 'N' THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END) AS is_independent
FROM subject_offered so
WHERE
  -- canonical filter for independent activities: explicit cluster or form type labeling as Independent Activity
  (so.CLUSTER_TYPE = 'Independent Activity' OR so.FORM_TYPE = 'Independent Activity')
  -- ensure we only return real section/activity instances with a section id
  AND so.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
independent_activity_sections.description: Rows representing activity/section records that are marked as independent activities (canonical filter only). One row per activity/section instance.

activity_supervisors.name: activity_supervisors
activity_supervisors.body_sql:
SELECT
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS person_id,
  lci.COURSE_NAME AS person_role,
  lci.COURSE_NAME AS subject_offering_id,
  opc.FULL_NAME AS name
FROM
  library_course_instructor AS lci
LEFT JOIN
  opa_person_current AS opc
    ON opc.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE = lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
activity_supervisors.description: Person-role assignments for activities/sections where the role indicates a supervisor/leader. One row per person-role assignment for an offering.

independent_activity_with_supervisor.name: independent_activity_with_supervisor
independent_activity_with_supervisor.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.`SUBJECT_TITLE`                                                         AS `subject_title`,
  so.`MEET_PLACE`                                                            AS `meet_place`,
  so.`TERM_CODE`                                                             AS `term_start_date`,
  opc.`FULL_NAME`                                                            AS `name`,
  so.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`                                           AS `subject_offering_id`,
  lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME`                                                      AS `person_id`
FROM
  `subject_offered` so
LEFT JOIN
  `library_course_instructor` lci
    ON lci.`COURSE_NAME` = so.`SUBJECT_TITLE`
    AND lci.`DATE_FROM` <= so.`TERM_CODE`
    AND (lci.`DATE_TO` IS NULL OR lci.`DATE_TO` >= so.`TERM_CODE`)
LEFT JOIN
  `opa_person_current` opc
    ON opc.`FULL_NAME` = lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME`
independent_activity_with_supervisor.description: Denormalized rows joining independent activity sections to their supervisor person rows (if any). One row per subject_offering + supervisor assignment.

employee_to_building_join.name: employee_to_building_join
employee_to_building_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  ed.MIT_ID                                   AS PERSON_ID,
  ed.FULL_NAME                                AS FULL_NAME,
  ed.OFFICE_LOCATION                          AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  NULL                                        AS ROOM,
  NULL                                        AS FLOOR,
  ed.OFFICE_LOCATION                          AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS                   AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  -- buildings table does not have CITY/STATE/POSTAL_CODE columns in this schema;
  -- postal/city/state exist on fac_building_address / fclt_building_address tables.
  -- To satisfy the required output columns coming from buildings, we attempt to pull them from buildings.
  -- If not present, they will be NULL here (per instruction not to substitute stored values from other tables).
  bld_addr.CITY                               AS CITY,
  bld_addr.STATE                              AS STATE,
  bld_addr.POSTAL_CODE                        AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM employee_directory AS ed
LEFT JOIN buildings AS b
  ON ed.OFFICE_LOCATION = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address AS bld_addr
  ON b.BUILDING_KEY = bld_addr.BUILDING_KEY
employee_to_building_join.description: Join of employee addresses to building rows on BUILDING_KEY to produce denormalized rows that combine employee room/floor and building address fields. Still does not apply the specific employee full-name or ADDRESS_PURPOSE filters.

ee_cs_subjects.name: ee_cs_subjects
ee_cs_subjects.body_sql:
SELECT

  so.SUBJECT_TITLE                       AS SUBJECT,
  so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME                     AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM subject_offered AS so
WHERE so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'
ee_cs_subjects.description: Rows for subjects that belong to the Electrical Eng & Computer Sci department (canonical subject/department membership).

rooms_with_full_name.name: rooms_with_full_name
rooms_with_full_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS ROOM_ID,
  -- Normalize FULL_ROOM_NAME: prefer ROOM_FULL_NAME from fac_rooms; if NULL, build from BUILDING_KEY + '/' + FLOOR + '/' + ROOM
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME, ''),
    CONCAT_WS('/', fr.BUILDING_KEY, NULLIF(fr.FLOOR,''), NULLIF(fr.ROOM,''))
  ) AS FULL_ROOM_NAME,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BLDG_ID
FROM fac_rooms fr
rooms_with_full_name.description: Canonical room rows with a distinct FULL_ROOM_NAME and room-to-building key; normalize NULLs and ensure a consistent full-room identifier.

parsed_room_building_identifiers.name: parsed_room_building_identifiers
parsed_room_building_identifiers.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.`MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  NULL AS ROOM,
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID_dup,
  cso.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  NULL AS ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  NULL AS FORMAT,
  cso.`TERM_DURATION` AS TERM_DURATION,
  -- parsed building number/code extracted from MEET_PLACE using common patterns:
  -- try "BldgName Room", "BUILDING_NUMBER-ROOM", "BUILDING_NUMBER ROOM", "BUILDING_NUMBER/ROOM", or leading token that looks like building number
  TRIM(
    NULLIF(
      NULLIF(
        -- pattern: token before first space if it matches letters+digits or digits
        REGEXP_SUBSTR(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '^[A-Za-z0-9#\-]+'),
        ''
      ),
      ''
    )
  ) AS parsed_building_code,
  -- normalized room: everything after a separator like space, dash, slash, or comma, or the trailing token that looks like room number
  TRIM(
    CASE
      WHEN cso.`MEET_PLACE` IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN cso.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '^[A-Za-z0-9#\\-]+[\\s\\-/,]+(.+)$' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '^[A-Za-z0-9#\\-]+[\\s\\-/,]+(.+)$', '\\1')
      WHEN cso.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '[\\s\\-/,]+[A-Za-z0-9#\\-]+$' THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '[A-Za-z0-9#\\-]+$')
      ELSE cso.`MEET_PLACE`
    END
  ) AS normalized_room
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
parsed_room_building_identifiers.description: Normalize and extract building identifier and room number from meeting-place fields (e.g., MEET_PLACE or ROOM) so building key/linking field is available. Produce one row per SECTION_ID with parsed building_number/building_code and normalized room string.

building_addresses_street.name: building_addresses_street
building_addresses_street.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  addr.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  addr.CITY AS CITY,
  addr.STATE AS STATE,
  addr.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address addr
  ON addr.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
WHERE addr.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'
building_addresses_street.description: One row per building address record for addresses purpose 'STREET', providing building key and street address components for joins to rooms/buildings.

room_floor_and_building_key.name: room_floor_and_building_key
room_floor_and_building_key.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- fac_rooms columns (carry through as-is)
  `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY`                                                  AS `ROOM_ID`,
  `fac_rooms`.`ROOM`                                                          AS `ROOM_NUMBER`,
  `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY`                                                  AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR`                                                         AS `FLOOR`,

  -- fclt_rooms columns (carry through as-is)
  `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY`                                                AS `FCLT_ROOM_ID`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`ROOM`                                                         AS `FCLT_ROOM_NUMBER`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`                                            AS `FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`FLOOR`                                                        AS `FCLT_FLOOR`,

  -- space_unit2.room identifiers (carry through as-is)
  `space_unit2`.`SPACE_UNIT_KEY`                                              AS `space_unit2_room_id`,

  -- space_floor.floor (carry through as-is)
  `space_floor`.`FLOOR`                                                       AS `space_floor_floor`,

  -- space_detail.room id (carry through as-is)
  `space_detail`.`BUILDING_ROOM`                                              AS `space_detail_room_id`
FROM `fac_rooms`
LEFT JOIN `fclt_rooms`
  ON `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` = `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY`
  -- also attempt join by room/building pair if the PK keys don't match
  OR (
       `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` = `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`
       AND `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` = `fclt_rooms`.`ROOM`
     )
LEFT JOIN `space_detail`
  ON `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` = `space_detail`.`BUILDING_KEY`
  AND `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR_KEY` = `space_detail`.`FLOOR_KEY`
  AND `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` = `space_detail`.`BUILDING_ROOM`
LEFT JOIN `space_unit2`
  ON `space_detail`.`SPACE_UNIT_KEY` = `space_unit2`.`SPACE_UNIT_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `space_floor`
  ON `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR_KEY` = `space_floor`.`FLOOR_KEY`
room_floor_and_building_key.description: Map room or meet_place (parsed) to building key and floor. One row per room record (room identifier) with floor and building key from facilities/space tables to associate sections with physical building and floor.

subject_base.name: subject_base
subject_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS subject,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE AS title
FROM subject_offered AS so
subject_base.description: One row per course subject (subject offered) with its canonical subject title to serve as the subject dimension for joining materials. Does not apply question-specific filters.

material_base.name: material_base
material_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key for grain/joinability
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS `id`,

  -- title: prefer the catalog title from library_reserve_catalog when available,
  -- but per instructions the required output column library_reserve_matrl_detail.title must come from that exact table.
  -- The library_reserve_matrl_detail table does not have a TITLE column in the schema, so join to library_reserve_catalog
  -- and expose its CATALOG_TITLE while still naming the output column `title`.
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS `title`,

  -- isbn: required as library_reserve_matrl_detail.isbn. The detail table does not contain ISBN in the DDL,
  -- so join to library_reserve_catalog and expose its CATALOG_ISBN as the view's isbn.
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_ISBN` AS `isbn`,

  -- cost: the tip_material table has price columns. The detail table does not contain a cost column in the DDL,
  -- so join to tip_material and expose NEW_SHELF_PRICE as the cost column in this view.
  -- Note: literals should be lifted out of the view; here we simply expose stored price column.
  `tip_material`.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE` AS `cost`,

  -- is_new flag: determine from tip_material.MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE or from existence of NEW_SHELF_PRICE.
  -- The detail table does not have an is_new column; expose a boolean-like integer (1/0).
  CASE
    WHEN `tip_material`.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE` IS NOT NULL THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS `is_new`,

  -- carry-through keys to keep joinable and for transparency
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`TERM_CODE`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS `library_reserve_matrl_detail_WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`,

  `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS `library_reserve_catalog_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_YEAR`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_PUBLISHER`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_CALL_NUMBER`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_SYSTEM_NUMBER`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_RECORD_UPDATE_DATE`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`RECORD_COUNTER`,

  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`,
  `tip_material`.`ISBN` AS `tip_material_ISBN`,
  `tip_material`.`TITLE` AS `tip_material_TITLE`,
  `tip_material`.`AUTHOR` AS `tip_material_AUTHOR`,
  `tip_material`.`EDITION` AS `tip_material_EDITION`,
  `tip_material`.`PUBLISHER` AS `tip_material_PUBLISHER`,
  `tip_material`.`YEAR` AS `tip_material_YEAR`,
  `tip_material`.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`,
  `tip_material`.`RENTAL_NEW_PRICE`,
  `tip_material`.`RENTAL_USED_PRICE`,
  `tip_material`.`MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE`

FROM `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `tip_material`
  -- join tip_material by ISBN if available; keep left join to preserve grain
  ON (`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_ISBN` IS NOT NULL
      AND `tip_material`.`ISBN` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_ISBN`)
material_base.description: One row per material (reserve/material/catalog entry) with material title, ISBN, cost, and a flag/column indicating whether the material is 'new'. This is the material dimension; do not filter by 'new' here to keep the view general (flag must be exposed).

subject_material_link.name: subject_material_link
subject_material_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrm.SUBJECT_ID                                 AS subject_offered_id,
  lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY                AS material_id,
  lrm.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY              AS LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,
  lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY                AS LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY,
  lrm.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY                AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  lrm.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY                AS LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY,
  lrm.TERM_CODE                                   AS TERM_CODE,
  lrm.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE                         AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM library_reserve_matrl_detail lrm
JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
subject_material_link.description: Mapping rows that associate subjects (courses) to materials (reserve/material entries). One row per subject-to-material association to enable joining subjects to their materials.

building_basic_info.name: building_basic_info
building_basic_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_ID,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- Parse DATE_BUILT from possible formats in source tables; must come from buildings.DATE_BUILT but that column doesn't exist in buildings table.
  -- Requirement: If required table.column is not available from that exact table, JOIN that base table to get it.
  -- The canonical DATE_BUILT exists on fac_building, fclt_building, fclt_building_hist; we'll prefer fac_building.DATE_BUILT when available for the building via BUILDING_NUMBER mapping.
  -- Preserve original stored DATE_BUILT column value (do not re-derive). Expose it as BUILDINGS.DATE_BUILT by selecting from the source table fac_building and aliasing to DATE_BUILT.
  fb.DATE_BUILT AS DATE_BUILT
FROM
  buildings b
  LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
    ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER

semantic_filters.buildings.DATE_BUILT: NOT NULL and parseable with format %m/%d/%Y

building_basic_info.description: Canonicalized building rows with parsed build year (when DATE_BUILT is a valid %m/%d/%Y date) and the building long name.

building_rows.name: building_rows
building_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  -- normalize empty string to NULL for BUILDING_NAME so downstream joins see a canonical null
  NULLIF(TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME`), '') AS `BUILDING_NAME`
FROM `buildings`
building_rows.description: One canonical row per building from the buildings table, exposing the building identifier and name for downstream joins. Normalize any NULL/empty name handling here if needed.

building_course_counts.name: building_course_counts
building_course_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  c.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  c.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  c.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  COUNT(DISTINCT
    CASE
      WHEN c.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND c.SUBJECT_ID <> '' THEN CONCAT('S|', c.SUBJECT_ID, '|', COALESCE(c.SUBJECT_NUMBER, ''))
      ELSE CONCAT('M|', COALESCE(c.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, ''))
    END
  ) AS course_count
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog c
  /* join all courses to every building to allow counting distinct courses per building.
     There is no direct mapping table provided in the schema, so this LEFT JOIN will produce
     zero-matches for buildings with no related course rows; courses without building context
     will not be assigned to any building. If you have a mapping table (e.g. rooms -> courses),
     replace this join with the appropriate mapping. */
  ON 1 = 0
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME,
  c.SUBJECT_ID,
  c.SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  c.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
building_course_counts.description: For each building (BUILDING_KEY), count distinct CIS courses mapped to that building. Distinctness is determined by the course identifier: (SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_NUMBER) when SUBJECT_ID is present, otherwise MASTER_SUBJECT_ID. Include buildings with zero matched courses (left join semantics should be applied when implementing).

buildings_raw_rows.name: buildings_raw_rows
buildings_raw_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  `BUILDING_NAME` AS BUILDING_NAME,
  `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  `BUILDING_COUNTER` AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  `BUILDING_NUMBER` AS BUILDING_CODE
FROM `buildings`
buildings_raw_rows.description: Select raw rows from the buildings table (no top-k or aggregation). This isolates the source cohort and allows downstream cleaning and filtering.

buildings_numeric_capacity.name: buildings_numeric_capacity
buildings_numeric_capacity.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_CODE,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- normalize: accept only integer-like positive values; else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRUNCATE(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0) = b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
         AND b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE >= 0
      THEN CAST(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  CASE
    WHEN b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRUNCATE(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0) = b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
         AND b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE >= 0
      THEN CAST(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- BUILDING_COUNTER is already integer typed in source; keep as-is but NULL if negative
  CASE
    WHEN b.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN b.BUILDING_COUNTER >= 0 THEN b.BUILDING_COUNTER
    ELSE NULL
  END AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM buildings b
buildings_numeric_capacity.description: Normalize candidate capacity columns into integer-typed columns and mark null/invalid values as NULL. Keep one row per building. Do not apply the selection of which capacity column to use for ranking here.

buildings_chosen_capacity.name: buildings_chosen_capacity
buildings_chosen_capacity.body_sql:
SELECT
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER`    AS `BUILDING_CODE`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME`      AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`   AS `BUILDING_COUNTER`,
  `buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,
  `buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`     AS `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,
  CASE
    WHEN `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) <> ''
         AND `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$'
    THEN 'BUILDING_COUNTER'
    WHEN `buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR)) <> ''
         AND CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$'
    THEN 'BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE'
    WHEN `buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR)) <> ''
         AND CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$'
    THEN 'BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `CHOSEN_CAPACITY_COLUMN`,
  CASE
    WHEN `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) <> ''
         AND `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$'
    THEN CAST(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS SIGNED)
    WHEN `buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR)) <> ''
         AND CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$'
    THEN CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS SIGNED)
    WHEN `buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR)) <> ''
         AND CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS CHAR) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$'
    THEN CAST(`buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `CHOSEN_CAPACITY_VALUE`
FROM `buildings`
buildings_chosen_capacity.description: For each building choose the single numeric capacity value to be used for comparisons following preference: BUILDING_COUNTER if non-null and integer-like, otherwise BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE if non-null and integer-like, otherwise BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE if non-null and integer-like. Produce one row per building with the chosen numeric capacity column name and its integer value. Do not apply top-k selection.

buildings_capacity_rank.name: buildings_capacity_rank
buildings_capacity_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_CODE,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  /* capacity_value chosen here is BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE (lifted out as literal choice) */
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS capacity_value,
  /* rank buildings by capacity_value desc, ties get same rank */
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE DESC) AS capacity_rank
FROM
  buildings b
buildings_capacity_rank.description: Rank buildings by the chosen capacity value in descending order and mark ties so the final query can return all buildings that share the maximum capacity.

buildings_with_numeric_floor.name: buildings_with_numeric_floor
buildings_with_numeric_floor.body_sql:
SELECT
  `BUILDING_KEY` AS `building_id`,
  `BUILDING_NAME` AS `building_name`,
  `BUILDING_COUNTER` AS `building_counter`
FROM `buildings`
WHERE `BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(`BUILDING_COUNTER`) <> ''
  AND CAST(`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS CHAR) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$'
buildings_with_numeric_floor.description: One row per building with a canonical numeric floor/count value parsed from the buildings table; exclude rows where the floor/count is NULL or not numeric.

max_building_floor_value.name: max_building_floor_value
max_building_floor_value.description: Single-row measure per database (no grouping keys) giving the maximum numeric building_counter across normalized buildings rows.

iap_cleaned_numeric_fields.name: iap_cleaned_numeric_fields
iap_cleaned_numeric_fields.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  so.TERM_CODE AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  cat.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS CATEGORY_TITLE,
  -- normalize enrollment: use SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER (int) if present else NULL; cast to SIGNED to enforce numeric
  CAST(so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER AS SIGNED) AS ENROLLMENT,
  -- normalize fee: use iap.FEE (int) cast to signed
  CAST(iap.FEE AS SIGNED) AS FEE_CHARGED
FROM subject_offered AS so
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail AS iap
  ON so.TERM_CODE = iap.TERM_CODE
  AND so.SUBJECT_ID = iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category AS cat
  ON iap.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = cat.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
WHERE
  -- ensure enrollment and fee cast successfully to numeric by checking they are not NULL after casts
  -- SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER is stored as int; FEE is stored as int; still enforce non-null
  so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
  AND iap.FEE IS NOT NULL
  -- exclude rows where SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY is NULL since grain is per SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID
  AND so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY IS NOT NULL
iap_cleaned_numeric_fields.description: Normalize and cast enrollment and fee fields to numeric types, and canonicalize IAP category name/identifier. Expose only rows where enrollment and fee cast successfully to numeric (exclude non-numeric).

iap_sessions_base.name: iap_sessions_base
iap_sessions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  iap_subject_session.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,
  iap_subject_session.SESSION_DATE AS SESSION_TERM,
  iap_subject_session.HAS_SESSION_INFO AS HAS_SESSION_INFO,
  iap_subject_detail.ENROLLMENT_TYPE AS ENROLLMENT,
  iap_subject_detail.FEE AS FEE,
  iap_subject_sponsor.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY AS SPONSOR_ID
FROM iap_subject_session
-- join to detail to get stored enrollment and fee columns (do not re-derive)
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail
  ON iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = iap_subject_session.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
-- join to sponsor to get sponsor id (as required from that table)
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor
  ON iap_subject_sponsor.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
-- restrict to rows whose term indicates IAP. Lift literal out: caller should replace 'IAP' with proper term code pattern if needed.
WHERE COALESCE(iap_subject_session.SESSION_DATE, '') <> ''
  AND iap_subject_session.SESSION_DATE LIKE CONCAT('%', 'IAP', '%')
iap_sessions_base.description: Rows representing individual IAP sessions (Independent Activities Period). Select only sessions whose term/term_type indicates IAP. Keep one row per session instance.

iap_sponsors.name: iap_sponsors
iap_sponsors.description: Canonical list of sponsors (sponsor id → sponsor display name). One row per sponsor identifier. This normalizes sponsor names for joins.

iap_session_with_sponsor.name: iap_session_with_sponsor
iap_session_with_sponsor.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY                                    AS SESSION_ID,
  sd.TERM_CODE                                                  AS SESSION_TERM,
  s.HAS_SESSION_INFO                                            AS HAS_SESSION_INFO,
  sd.ENROLLMENT_TYPE                                             AS ENROLLMENT,
  sd.FEE                                                        AS FEE,
  sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY                                    AS SPONSOR_ID,
  sp.SPONSOR_NAME                                               AS SPONSOR_NAME
FROM iap_subject_session s
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail sd
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor sp
  ON sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
iap_session_with_sponsor.description: Denormalized IAP session rows joined to their sponsor names. One row per session with sponsor metadata (may be NULL if sponsor missing).

employee_directory_persons.name: employee_directory_persons
employee_directory_persons.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_PERSON_ID,
  d.EMAIL_ADDRESS AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  d.FULL_NAME AS FULL_NAME
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
employee_directory_persons.description: All individuals from the employee directory that may be matched to instructors; canonicalize key identifiers (MIT ID) and provide contact fields used for final output.

person_academic_year_iap_rollup.name: person_academic_year_iap_rollup
person_academic_year_iap_rollup.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_PERSON_ID,
  s.SESSION_DATE AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SUBJECT_ID,
  s.SESSION_DESCRIPTION AS FEE,
  s.SESSION_START_TIME AS ENROLLMENT
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
JOIN iap_subject_session s
  ON 1=1
person_academic_year_iap_rollup.description: Per employee (by MIT_PERSON_ID) and academic year, compute counts of distinct IAP subjects, min/max fee among their IAP offerings for that year, and sum of enrollment across those offerings.

term_descriptions.name: term_descriptions
term_descriptions.description: Canonical term rows providing TERM_CODE and human-readable TERM_DESCRIPTION for academic terms, to be joined to session rows.

iap_term_aggregates.name: iap_term_aggregates
iap_term_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  SUM(COALESCE(sd.FEE, 0)) AS FEE,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.SESSION_NUMBER) AS ENROLLMENT
FROM subject_iap_schedule s
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail sd
  ON s.TERM_CODE = sd.TERM_CODE
GROUP BY s.TERM_CODE
iap_term_aggregates.description: Per TERM_CODE aggregates for IAP sessions: count of sessions, sum of fees, min and max enrollment. Built from cleaned numeric IAP session rows.
